facts.statement: Wuttagoonaspis was a primitive arthrodire placoderm fish that lived in Australia during the Middle Devonian.
facts.quote: Wuttagoonaspis is an extinct genus of primitive arthrodire placoderm fish from the Middle Devonian of Australia.

facts.statement: The animal had a box-like skull measuring up to 18 centimeters in length and a median dorsal plate averaging 10 centimeters.
facts.quote: The box-like skull is up to 18 centimeters in length, and the median dorsal plate averages in length about 10 centimeters.

facts.statement: The type species Wuttagoonaspis fletcheri was described by Ritchie in 1973.
The species Wuttagoonaspis milligani was described by Young and Goujet in 2003.
facts.quote: Wuttagoonaspis milligani, described by Young and Goujet in 2003.

facts.statement: Wuttagoonaspis belongs to the family Wuttagoonaspidae and is closely related to the genus Yiminaspis.
facts.quote: Wuttagoonaspis belongs to the family Wuttagoonaspidae, and is closely related to Yiminaspis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Wuttagoonaspis date from the Pragian to the Eifelian stages, between 413.02 and 387.95 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pragian to Eifelian (413.02 to 387.95 million years ago)
